answer: A farm hence spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the echo quota and the knoll admission check. Admission is capped at 5 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. Because the terrace audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 12 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
